- "OS-level isolation per agent. No noisy neighbours." (isolated containers per agent)
- "Keys live in a gateway. The agent never sees them." (credential gateway)
- "Approval before action" for sensitive operations; "Full audit trail"
- "Walls between workspaces… Cross-workspace reads are architecturally impossible"
- Value prop: "One AI. Four lives. The same memory — anywhere you write" — one assistant across web, WhatsApp, and "Skills," with a shared private profile ("Your tastes, your people, your tone").

This matches the described "consumer product built on a containerized-agent stack with privacy-by-architecture positioning."

**Onboarding (from the same page):** ~60 seconds, three steps: (1) Sign in with Google (no password stored, no card), (2) "Name it" — a private container is created in seconds, (3) start writing on web or WhatsApp; Skills added later. Tagline: "Up and running before your tea cools." **Notably, no interview/calibration step is advertised** — it's a minimal-friction "name it and start talking" flow.

**Uncertainty marker:** I could verify only what the sites themselves say; I found no independent press coverage, funding announcements, or third-party reviews of Solela, so company scale/maturity is unverified. Search results also surface an unrelated similarly-named company, **Sola (sola.ai)**, an a16z-backed automation startup (https://www.sola.ai/, https://a16z.com/announcement/investing-in-sola/) — do not conflate the two.

---

## TASK 1: Onboarding-by-interview / calibration patterns

### 1. Lindy.ai — role-based questions + templates, not a deep interview
A hands-on walkthrough (https://obviostudio.substack.com/p/ai-integration-lindy-from-onboarding) reports: after signup Lindy asks about **your role/industry** ("I chose freelancer, and boom — freelancing tools front and center"), then lands you on a dashboard pre-populated with **role-matched templates** and "a full example workflow ready to go." Lindy also offers "a custom agent setup right away" via a scheduled call (human-assisted, not AI-interview). Agents themselves are built conversationally ("Chat with Lindy," https://docs.lindy.ai/skills/by-lindy/chat-with-lindy), and Lindy sells onboarding-agent templates to others (https://www.lindy.ai/templates/client-onboarding-agent). **Pattern: light segmentation question → templates, plus conversational agent-building; no self-profiling interview.**

### 2. Martin (trymartin.com) — connect-accounts onboarding, memory built through use
Per third-party reviews and the product docs (https://tooldirectory.ai/tools/martin, https://docs.trymartin.com/introduction, https://chatgate.ai/post/martin/): onboarding is fast self-serve — sign up (web/iOS), access code, connect email + Google/Outlook calendar, phone, optional Slack/WhatsApp; ~5–10 minutes. Personalization comes from a "custom memory architecture" that learns preferences **over time in use**, not from an upfront interview (https://venturebeat.com/ai/these-yale-and-berkeley-dropouts-just-raised-2-million-to-build-an-ai-assistant-that-could-rival-openai). I found **no evidence of an intake interview or onboarding phone call**; the onboarding URL (https://app.trymartin.com/onboarding) is auth-gated so I could not inspect the flow directly — flag as unverified detail. **Pattern: integrations-first, ambient learning.**

### 3. Ohai.ai — structured setup wizard, no interview
From https://www.ohai.ai/how-it-works/: Step 1 "Set up your account in minutes. Add your name, choose your preferences, and connect your Google, Apple, or Outlook calendars," join/create a household "Circle"; Step 2 forward emails/screenshots/PDFs to the assistant "O"; Step 3 it "turns your updates into a clear and actionable plan." The page shows **no conversational preference interview** — it's a forms-and-connections wizard where the assistant learns from forwarded artifacts. **Pattern: connect-your-data onboarding; calibration by ingestion, not conversation.**

### 4. Yohana (Panasonic) — human-guide intake, tech-assisted
Yohana matches members with human "Yo Assistants" plus "a dedicated guide" and specialists; Panasonic materials describe families being "paired with a guide to map their goals" (https://www.yohana.com/about-us, https://news.panasonic.com/global/stories/12497, https://stripe.com/newsroom/stories/yohana-and-stripe). Behind the scenes, data systems "tailor solutions to each member's preferences" and learn from every completed to-do (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/yoky-matsuoka-launches-yohana-new-wellness-company-for-moms--families-301372112.html, https://www.geekwire.com/2021/robotics-pioneer-yoky-matsuokas-panasonic-venture-debuts-personal-assistant-service-seattle/). **Uncertainty:** yohana.com/how-it-works returned 502 and GeekWire 403, so the exact intake mechanics (survey vs. call) are from secondary snippets — medium confidence. **Pattern: the interview exists but is done by humans; the closest "concierge intake" analog.**

### 5. AI coaching products — the clearest interview-to-calibration examples
- **BetterUp:** first-login onboarding (5–10 min) with preference/topic selection; a 2–3 minute **Intake Survey** "helps to get to know them and match them with a Coach"; the **Whole Person Assessment** (30 dimensions) feeds personalization — for AI Coach users it's optional, nudged by the AI coach itself (https://support.betterup.com/hc/en-us/articles/36688702739611-BetterUp-AI-Coach, https://support.betterup.com/hc/en-us/articles/360049794271-The-Whole-Person-Assessment).
- **Valence "Nadia":** builds a personalization layer ("knows coaching, knows your company, knows you"); every conversation enriches memory; Nadia can generate a **"collaboration profile"** — a how-to-work-with-me document under user control that other Nadias can read (https://www.valence.co/videos/ai-first-coaching-with-nadia-summit-2026, https://www.bvp.com/news/meet-nadia-valences-ai-coach-for-leadership-development-and-workplace-collaboration). Gilead's deployment note: getting users **into a live Nadia session within 10 minutes** produced the "aha" — participants "felt Nadia was getting to know them" (https://www.valence.co/ai-and-the-workforce/how-gilead-sciences-is-scaling-ai-coaching-to-all-employees-kerry-okeeffe-gilead-valence). Calibration-through-conversation rather than upfront forms.
- **Rocky.ai:** onboarding "asks thoughtful questions about your goals, obstacles, and past successes" (third-party review: https://aicompanionguides.com/blog/rocky-ai-review-motivation-coach/); platform includes a Self-Assessment Builder and benchmark tests (https://www.rocky.ai/).
- **Dot (New Computer)** — the purest consumer example of onboarding-by-interview: onboarding asked "a good handful of getting-to-know-you questions" ("What do you do for work?", "How do you spend a typical Sunday?") then probed deeper based on answers, building a persistent psychological profile (https://techcrunch.com/2024/06/21/dots-ai-really-really-wants-to-get-to-know-you/, https://www.fastcompany.com/90975882/meet-dot-an-ai-companion-designed-by-an-apple-alum-here-to-help-you-live-your-best-life). **Cautionary note: Dot shut down in October 2025** (https://techcrunch.com/2025/09/05/personalized-ai-companion-app-dot-is-shutting-down/) — interview-depth personalization alone didn't sustain the business.

### 6. "Agent interviews you, then builds the workflow" mechanisms
- **OpenAI GPT Builder:** the canonical implementation — a conversational builder that asks clarifying questions as you describe the GPT, then drafts name, avatar, instructions, and conversation starters; a Configure tab holds the result (https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8770868-gpt-builder, https://zapier.com/blog/custom-chatgpt/).
- **Zapier Agents / Copilot:** describe the agent in natural language ("qualify incoming leads and route them…"); a **prompt assistant refines your instructions** and Copilot builds the configured agent — "feels more like having a conversation than programming" (https://zapier.com/blog/zapier-agents-guide/, https://zapier.com/blog/how-to-create-ai-agents/).
- **Relevance AI / Dust.tt:** searches did not surface evidence of an interview-style setup for either — both appear to use form/template-based agent configuration. Explicitly marking this as **not found**, not as absence-proven.

### 7. UX research: what actually activates/retains non-technical users
- **Templates beat blank canvas — near-universal convergence.** An analysis of 150+ AI product onboarding flows found "nearly every successful AI company has converged on the same activation strategy": template activation loops; the blank canvas ("blinking cursor") kills conversion; **generated drafts** outperform even static templates because "users react faster to something editable than to a completely empty workspace" (https://www.fishmanafnewsletter.com/p/how-ai-products-drive-adoption-in-onboarding-through-template-activation-loop).
- **Light questioning works; heavy interviews are rare.** Growthmates' teardown: winners deliver a wow moment within ~3 minutes; light role/goal questions (Synthesia) make users feel the product was "built for someone like you"; but "almost nobody" asks about AI experience level, and most products can't tell whether users actually hit an aha moment (https://www.growthmates.news/p/what-ai-products-get-right-and-wrong).
- **Sub-60-second activation** is the emerging bar for AI onboarding (https://productled.com/blog/ai-onboarding); example prompts/premade dialogues "dramatically reduced drop-off at the first interaction" for low-AI-familiarity users (https://userpilot.com/blog/onboarding-ux-examples/).
- **Full activation is multi-session:** activation metrics correlate more with month-2/3 renewals than first purchase (Fishman, same source).

### Synthesis
The market splits into three calibration patterns: **(a) interview-first** (Dot, coaching intakes, GPT Builder) — strongest personalization signal, but Dot's shutdown shows it doesn't guarantee retention; **(b) template/segmentation-first** (Lindy, Zapier) — the empirically dominant activation pattern; **(c) ingestion/ambient-first** (Martin, Ohai, Solela) — connect accounts, learn from use. The research consensus favors a hybrid: 1–3 light calibration questions + a generated editable draft, with deep profiling deferred into the first real sessions (the Nadia/Gilead model) rather than a long upfront interview.

**Relay.app** — The most developed per-step HITL toolkit among the no-code platforms: dedicated step types — **Approvals**, **Get data input** (typed form to assignee), **Complete a task** — plus a one-toggle **AI output review** (output routed to email/Slack for approve/revise before the run continues), with interactive Slack approval. Docs: https://docs.relay.app/human-in-the-loop/human-in-the-loop-steps and https://docs.relay.app/human-in-the-loop/ai-output-reviews. HITL is Relay's marketed differentiator (https://www.relay.app/features/human-in-the-loop), but it's static per-workflow design, not graduated trust.

### Enterprise agent platforms (governance/permission model)

**Salesforce Agentforce** — Layered model: user-defined guardrails + Salesforce-managed protections + Einstein Trust Layer; agent data access is permissions-based per agent type/action; guardrails specify when to **escalate to a human**, and actions can orchestrate approval workflows (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000372857&language=en_US&type=3, https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/trusted-agentic-ai/explore-agentforce-guardrails-and-trust-patterns, https://architect.salesforce.com/fundamentals/agentic-patterns). This is scoped-permission + escalation, not autonomy levels.

**Microsoft Copilot Studio / M365** — The heaviest governance apparatus: admin **approval before agents are made available**, enable/disable/assign/block per user/group in the M365 admin center (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/manage/manage-copilot-agents-integrated-apps, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/microsoft-365/agent-essentials/m365-agents-admin-guide), DLP policies, and Copilot Studio security/governance controls (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/security-and-governance). In 2026 Microsoft shipped **Agent 365**, a "centralized control plane" for agent inventory, permissions, behavior, and activity (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot/blog/copilot-studio/new-and-improved-agent-governance-intelligent-workflows-and-connected-app-experiences/). This governs *which agents exist and what they can touch* — organizational trust, not per-agent graduated autonomy.

### Coding agents / computer-use agents (explicit autonomy modes — the closest to real "levels")

**Claude Code** — Discrete permission modes (default / plan / acceptEdits / dontAsk / bypassPermissions) plus persistent allow/ask/deny rules in settings.json, evaluated deny→ask→allow (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions). Notably, "always allow" grants **persist**, so the effective autonomy envelope genuinely widens over time — but by user accretion, not automatic graduation.

**Cursor** — Two mechanisms: (a) auto-run with a **command allowlist** (non-listed commands still require confirmation); a security critique of the denylist approach exists (https://www.backslash.security/blog/cursor-ai-security-flaw-autorun-denylist); (b) **Auto-review** (June 11, 2026): a classifier agent in the execution path evaluates each action against user intent, explicitly marketed as making autonomy "a dial, not a switch" — free movement when stakes are low, slowdown at meaningful boundaries. It blocks ~4% of reviewed actions; only ~7% of chats hit a user interruption vs prior ~40% blocking at some enterprises. Now default for new users (https://cursor.com/blog/agent-autonomy-auto-review). This is *contextual* autonomy, not earned-over-time autonomy — the post frames it as adaptive refinement, not progressive expansion.

**Devin (Cognition)** — CLI has mode cycling: /normal, /accept-edits, /plan, /bypass; agent profiles (normal/plan/ask) and permission modes are two independent controls (https://docs.devin.ai/cli/reference/commands, https://cli.devin.ai/docs/changelog/stable). Same family as Claude Code's modes.

**OpenAI Operator / ChatGPT agent** — Trained to ask **explicit confirmation before consequential actions** (purchases); **Watch Mode** requires active supervision on sensitive sites (email, financial); **takeover mode** for credentials (https://openai.com/index/introducing-operator/, https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11752874-chatgpt-agent, https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-agent/). This is risk-tiered oversight baked in — three de facto trust tiers (auto / watched / human-only) keyed to site sensitivity, but fixed by OpenAI, not earned.

### Confidence-threshold customer-support agents

**Intercom Fin** — Publishes ~51% average autonomous resolution; escalates via handover when it can't resolve (https://myaskai.com/blog/intercom-fin-ai-agent-complete-guide-2026). **Sierra** — "built for high autonomy" with bespoke, engineering-configured escalation logic (https://quiq.com/blog/sierra-ai-vs-decagon/). **Decagon** — Agent Operating Procedures (natural-language agent logic) + **Watchtower** monitoring; its recommended rollout is explicitly graduated: launch to a small **percentage of traffic**, monitor, then scale to 100% once success criteria are met (https://decagon.ai/blog/ai-customer-support-setup, https://myaskai.com/blog/decagon-ai-complete-guide-2026). **Shadow/draft-mode rollouts** — A widely-described pattern in support AI: AI drafts replies humans review → specific ticket types auto → full frontline (https://www.itsmautopilot.com/en/blog/shadow-mode-ai-rollout, https://cobbai.com/blog/ai-rollout-post-launch-review). This is the closest thing to operationalized "earned trust," but the graduation decision is human/process, not product-automated.

## 2. Frameworks & writeups

- **"Levels of Autonomy for AI Agents"** — Feng, McDonald & Zhang (arXiv June 2025, Knight First Amendment Institute): the canonical SAE-style framework. Five levels defined by **user role**: L1 Operator → L2 Collaborator → L3 Consultant → L4 Approver → L5 Observer. Argues autonomy is a *design decision separable from capability*, and proposes **"autonomy certificates"** as a governance mechanism (https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12469, https://knightcolumbia.org/content/levels-of-autonomy-for-ai-agents-1).
- **Swarmia, "Five levels of AI coding agent autonomy"** (Mar 19, 2026): Assistive → Conversational → Task Agent → Autonomous Teammate → "Agentic Avalanche"; thesis: higher isn't better — match level to task ambiguity and pipeline maturity (https://www.swarmia.com/blog/five-levels-ai-agent-autonomy/).
- **Anthropic, "Measuring AI agent autonomy in practice"** (Feb 18, 2026) — the key empirical work: 80% of tool calls carry safeguards; 0.8% irreversible actions; and crucially, **autonomy grants grow with user experience** — full auto-approve in ~20% of new users' sessions vs >40% at 750+ sessions, while interrupt rates *rise* (5%→9%), i.e. oversight shifts from approval-based to monitoring-based (https://www.anthropic.com/research/measuring-agent-autonomy).
- **McKinsey**: "Seizing the agentic AI advantage" (https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/quantumblack/our-insights/seizing-the-agentic-ai-advantage) and agentic-AI governance / "Trust in the age of agents" (https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/risk-and-resilience/our-insights/trust-in-the-age-of-agents); EY CIO playbook (https://www.ey.com/en_us/ey-center-for-executive-leadership/defining-a-cio-playbook-on-agentic-ai); ManageEngine CIO playbook — start read-only/sandboxed, log override frequency, "expand execution privileges only after reversal rates decline" (https://insights.manageengine.com/artificial-intelligence/agentic-ai-autonomous-it-governance-playbook/); CDOTrends "Autonomy Is Earned" (https://www.cdotrends.com/story/4916/autonomy-earned-most-enterprise-ai-agents-havent-earned-it). Crawl-walk-run maturity models: Microsoft SOC guide (HITL for high-impact, human-on-the-loop for medium, autonomous for low once accuracy proven; "autonomy must be earned, not assumed") https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoft-security-blog/crawl-walk-run-a-practitioners-guide-to-ai-maturity-in-the-soc/4500433; nexocode maturity model https://nexocode.com/blog/posts/the-agentic-ai-maturity-model-crawl-walk-run-scale/. I did not find a dedicated a16z post on graduated autonomy — flagging that as not found rather than absent.
- **LangChain/LangGraph** — first-class HITL primitives: `interrupt` (https://www.langchain.com/blog/making-it-easier-to-build-human-in-the-loop-agents-with-interrupt) and HITL middleware with per-tool interrupt config — approve / edit / reject / respond, values True / False / InterruptOnConfig per tool (https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/human-in-the-loop). This gives builders the *substrate* for graduated autonomy (per-tool trust config) but no built-in graduation logic.
- Uncertain/unverified (surfaced in search, not fetched): arXiv "Bounded Autonomy for Enterprise AI: Typed Action Contracts" (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.14723) and "Autonomy and Agency in Agentic AI: Architectural Tactics for Regulated Contexts" (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.12105) — relevant-looking academic follow-ons, contents not verified.

## 3. Verdict

**Graduated trust exists as vocabulary and process; almost nowhere as an automated product mechanism.**

1. **What's actually shipped is overwhelmingly (a) per-step approval toggles** (Lindy, Relay, Zapier, LangGraph interrupts) **and (b) discrete global modes** (Claude Code, Devin, Cursor allowlists, Operator's watch/confirm tiers). These are static: the user or admin sets the trust level; nothing graduates on its own.

2. **Closest shipped approximations to graduated/expanding autonomy:**
   - **Cursor Auto-review** (June 2026) — the most explicit productization of "autonomy as a dial": a classifier dynamically modulates freedom per action based on stakes/intent. But it's *contextual*, not *earned-over-time* (https://cursor.com/blog/agent-autonomy-auto-review).
   - **Claude Code's persistent allowlists** — trust accretes as users grant "always allow" rules, so the autonomy envelope genuinely widens with tenure, but via manual grants.
   - **Decagon-style percentage-of-traffic ramps + shadow mode** in support AI — real graduated rollout, but the promotion decision is human (https://decagon.ai/blog/ai-customer-support-setup).

3. **Evidence that autonomy expands over time in practice is behavioral, not mechanical**: Anthropic's Feb 2026 measurement study shows users *themselves* graduate agents — auto-approve doubles from ~20% to >40% of sessions as experience grows, with oversight shifting to monitoring (https://www.anthropic.com/research/measuring-agent-autonomy). That's earned trust happening *in the user*, not in the product.

4. **No shipped product I could verify implements automatic earned autonomy** — i.e., "agent's permission scope widens automatically as its track record improves" (e.g., auto-promotion after N successful approvals, or reversal-rate-gated privilege expansion). That pattern exists only in consulting playbooks and governance writeups (ManageEngine, Microsoft SOC guide, CDOTrends). Marked with confidence: this is an absence-of-evidence claim after targeted searching, not proof of nonexistence — a vendor could ship this behind enterprise sales walls.

5. **Differentiator status**: HITL depth *is* marketed as a differentiator (Relay.app leads with it; Cursor leads with Auto-review; Microsoft leads with governance/Agent 365). But "trust levels that expand automatically" remains an open product gap as of July 2026 — the Feng/McDonald/Zhang "autonomy certificates" idea (https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12469) is the closest formal proposal and is not implemented anywhere I could verify.

## Category Verdict: Is the "digital employee" working?

**1. The fully autonomous AI SDR experiment of 2024–25 broadly failed.** Documented churn is brutal: 11x employees reported 70–80% customer loss (TechCrunch, above); category-wide analyses report **50–70% annual churn for AI SDR tools** — roughly double human-SDR-program churn — and a claim (attributed to Topo.io research) that only ~2% of implementations stick long-term (https://www.digitalapplied.com/blog/case-against-ai-sdrs-contrarian-analysis-2026, https://lucreya.com/articles/autonomous-ai-sdr-agents — secondary analyst posts, directionally consistent, individual numbers unverified). Failure modes cited for 2026: deliverability collapse, brand damage, intent-data noise, and a "18-month half-life" where reply rates decay 60%+ as buyers pattern-match AI templates (https://www.digitalapplied.com/blog/case-against-ai-sdrs-contrarian-analysis-2026).

**2. Broader AI-app retention is structurally worse than SaaS:** annual subscriber retention ~21% for AI apps vs ~31% non-AI (https://www.technewsworld.com/story/ai-apps-generate-revenue-but-struggle-with-retention-180236.html); ChartMogul has documented an "AI churn wave" in SaaS retention data (https://chartmogul.com/reports/saas-retention-the-ai-churn-wave/).

**3. The pattern separating winners from losers:**
- **Winners are bounded-task, verifiable-output products:** Devin/Cognition (code compiles or it doesn't; $25B valuation) and Piper/Qualified (inbound qualification of warm traffic; acquired by Salesforce Dec 2025). Both avoided the open-ended "replace a human's judgment" promise.
- **Losers/strugglers sold headcount replacement on open-ended judgment tasks:** 11x (scandal, CEO out), Cykel (£4K half-year revenue), MultiOn (pivoted to a reminders app).
- **The middle** (Artisan, Ema, Maisa, Lyzr, Beam) is repositioning: less "fire your team," more auditable copilots, human-in-the-loop, and platform/infrastructure framing.

**4. Emerging consensus (2026):** "The AI SDR is dead, long live the AI SDR" — the capability is being absorbed as a feature layer in existing sales stacks rather than surviving as standalone "employees"; every successful deployment keeps humans in the loop, and 36% of B2B companies that cut SDR teams in 2025 did so mostly via attrition, with a documented "rehire the humans" boomerang (https://www.commonroom.io/blog/common-room-ai-agent-pipeline-generation/, https://www.landbase.com/blog/death-of-bdr-role-ai-agents-sdr-hiring-2026, https://hrexecutive.com/the-ai-layoff-trap-why-half-will-be-quietly-rehired/). The "digital employee" *metaphor* increasingly looks like a marketing artifact of 2024; the products that endure are sold as tools with measurable, narrow outcomes.

**What it automates post-call:** A suite of "AI sales agents": a **CRM Auto-Update Agent** (auto-fills CRM fields / sales stages, "1-click" update), **follow-up email drafting** in the customer's voice from call insights (<60 sec, per vendor), coaching **scorecards**, real-time **Slack deal-risk alerts** to managers, and knowledge-base updates with human-in-the-loop verification (https://www.attention.com/product/ai-sales-agents, https://www.attention.com/). Integrates with 200+ tools incl. Salesforce, HubSpot, Gmail, Zoom (https://www.attention.com/).

**Configuration:** Customizable email templates and scheduling options; agents monitor calls for configured signals. Admin-vs-rep split is not clearly documented publicly — uncertainty flagged (https://www.attention.com/product/ai-sales-agents).

**Pricing:** Not public; demo-gated. Third-party estimates range ~$100–$500/user/mo, with one report of ~$1,600/user/year plans — treat all figures as unverified estimates (https://www.selecthub.com/p/conversation-intelligence-software/attention-com/, https://aihungry.com/tools/attention/pricing).

**Traction:** $14M Series A led by Alven, Oct 2024; angels include Dharmesh Shah and Adam D'Angelo (https://salestools.io/en/report/attention-14-million-series-a-october-2024). G2: 4.9/5 but only ~61 reviews — high satisfaction, small footprint relative to Gong/Fireflies (https://www.g2.com/products/attention/reviews). Customers cited: BambooHR, Preply, Unify, Abridge (https://www.attention.com/product/ai-sales-agents). One case study claims forecast error cut from 15% to 5% (vendor-reported).

---

## 3. Gong

**What it automates post-call:** In April 2025 Gong launched a portfolio of named AI agents (https://www.gong.io/press/gong-redefines-ai-agents-to-deliver-real-revenue-impact): post-call-relevant ones include **AI Tasker** (suggests next-action to-dos), **AI Composer** (drafts personalized follow-up emails), **AI Call Reviewer** (coaching against call assessments), **AI Deal Reviewer** (evaluates deals against sales methodologies — i.e., methodology-aware scoring rather than just field extraction), **AI Activity Mapper** (auto-links calls to accounts/contacts/opportunities), plus AI Briefer for handoffs/knowledge sharing. CRM field writing exists via "AI Data Extractor"-type capability that creates/updates CRM fields from conversation content (secondary sources: https://reply.io/blog/gong-ai-review/, https://www.oliv.ai/blog/gong-features — exact SKU naming here is less certain than the press-release agent names). At Celebrate (Oct 2025) the portfolio expanded to 18 agents incl. AI Deep Researcher and expanded Ask Anything (https://www.gong.io/press/gong-unveils-new-ai-innovations-to-help-revenue-teams-drive-growth-at-scale). June 2026 release notes add trigger-based auto-emailed account/deal briefs (https://help.gong.io/docs/our-monthly-updates).

**Configuration:** "Agent Studio" with drag-and-drop fields and pre-built templates; reps can also save Assistant prompts as reusable personal agents (https://www.gong.io/press/gong-redefines-ai-agents-to-deliver-real-revenue-impact). Mixed admin + rep-level model.

**Pricing:** Agents are "included with Gong licenses at no extra cost" (same press release) — but Gong base pricing is opaque and heavy: third-party benchmarks put Foundation at ~$1,600/user/yr, bundles $2,880–$3,000/user/yr, plus platform fees ($5K–$50K) and implementation ($15K–$65K); March 2025 unbundling raised effective per-user cost 25–56% (https://www.oliv.ai/blog/gong-io-pricing, https://www.sybill.ai/blogs/gong-pricing). All third-party estimates, not published list prices.

**Traction:** Gong self-reported ARR topping $500M with 55%+ YoY growth, 5,000+ customers, Gong Assistant usage up 200%+ YoY (press release, May 2026: https://www.gong.io/press/gong-growth-accelerates-past-55-yoy-arr-tops-500m — self-reported, unaudited; the 55% figure is surprisingly high for a company this size, treat cautiously). G2 4.7/5 across 6,500+ reviews; recurring complaint themes are pricing, forced bundling, and platform fees; one analysis notes ~40% of Gong customers also pay for Clari (https://www.sybill.ai/blogs/gong-reviews, https://www.oliv.ai/blog/gong-io-pricing). Competitor critique of the agent strategy exists (https://www.vivun.com/gong-agents-2025 — biased source).

---

## 4. Salesforce Agentforce (SDR + Sales Coach agents)

**What it automates:** These are less "post-call" and more "around-the-rep":
- **Agentforce SDR** autonomously nurtures inbound leads (answers questions, handles objections, books meetings, multi-channel incl. SMS/WhatsApp) and does the one true post-interaction automation in scope: a **warm handoff brief** summarizing lead info and prior interactions for the human seller (https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/einstein-sales-agents-announcement/).
- **Agentforce Sales Coach** does practice-based coaching: reps pick an opportunity stage and verbally pitch for up to 5 minutes; the agent role-plays and scores against best practices for five opportunity stages (Qualification → Negotiation) (https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/agentforce-for-sales-coaching-setup-and-customization/get-to-know-agentforce-sales-coach, https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=release-notes.rn_sales_agents_coach.htm&language=en_US&release=252&type=5).
- Notably, Agentforce does **not** ship a strong "call → CRM fields" post-call agent comparable to Momentum/Attention; call summarization lives in Einstein Conversation Insights, and Sales Coach requires Data Cloud.

**Configuration:** Admin-heavy: Setup in Salesforce, grounded in org CRM data, requires Data Cloud/Einstein provisioning; Trailhead modules exist for setup and customization (links above).

**Pricing:** Originally $2/conversation (backlash), replaced May 2025 by **Flex Credits**: 20 credits/action ≈ $0.10/action, $500 per 100K-credit pack, pay-as-you-go GA Aug 2025 (https://www.salesforce.com/news/press-releases/2025/05/15/agentforce-flexible-pricing-news/, https://aquiva.com/blog/agentforce-pricing-gets-a-long-overdue-fix-flex-credits-are-now-live). Sales Coach cited at $125/user/mo plus Data Cloud dependency (~$200–300 more) by a third party (https://www.oliv.ai/blog/agentforce-sales-coach — competitor source, verify before relying).

**Traction / failures:** The clearest documented adoption struggle in this set: Salesforce guided FY2026 revenue below expectations citing slower Agentforce adoption; ~12% of customers on an Agentforce deal, only ~6% paid; Q4 2025: 5,000 deals, 3,000 paid (https://www.salesforceben.com/where-are-we-really-at-with-agentforce-adoption/). Countervailing signal: 60%+ of Q4 FY26 Agentforce/Data 360 bookings from existing-customer expansion (https://www.salesforceben.com/agentforce-customers-are-doubling-down-60-of-q4-bookings-came-from-expansions/). Pricing-model whiplash is itself evidence of buyer resistance (https://www.getmonetizely.com/blogs/the-doomed-evolution-of-salesforces-agentforce-pricing).

---

## 5. HubSpot Breeze

**What it automates post-call:** The Spring 2025 agents (Customer, Prospecting, Knowledge Base, Content) were *not* post-call tools (https://www.hubspot.com/company-news/spring-2025-spotlight-breeze-agents). The post-call piece arrived with **Smart Deal Progression** (Spring 2026 Spotlight, public beta): after every rep-prospect call it analyzes the transcript plus full deal history and produces three outputs — **suggested CRM updates** (deal stage, amount, next steps, close date, outcome, applying your pipeline definitions and forecasting logic), a **drafted follow-up email**, and **action items** (https://www.hubspot.com/company-news/spring-2026-spotlight, https://www.hyphadev.io/blog/hubspot-spring-2026-spotlight). Note: "suggested" — human-approve, not autonomous writes.

**Configuration:** Native to Smart CRM; grounded in the org's own pipeline/stage definitions; Prospecting Agent uses admin-defined "selling profiles" (product/persona/market) (https://www.hubspot.com/company-news/spring-2025-spotlight-breeze-agents).

**Pricing:** HubSpot moved Breeze agents to **outcome-based pricing** (from April 14, 2026): Prospecting Agent $1.00 per lead recommended (was per-contact-enrolled monthly), Customer Agent $0.50 per *resolved* conversation (was $1.00/conversation); runs on HubSpot Credits; 28-day free trial (https://www.hubspot.com/company-news/hubspots-customer-agent-and-prospecting-agent-now-you-pay-when-the-task-is-complete, https://www.cmswire.com/customer-experience/hubspot-shifts-breeze-ai-agents-to-pay-per-result-pricing/). Smart Deal Progression pricing in beta not published — uncertain.

**Traction:** Prospecting Agent activations up 57% QoQ per HubSpot (self-reported, same announcement). The repricing to pay-per-result is itself a strong buyer-behavior signal (see synthesis).

---

## 6. Day.ai

**What it automates post-call:** An AI-native CRM ("CRMx" — context graph) rather than a bolt-on: it joins Zoom/Meet/Teams calls, transcribes, and then **auto-builds and maintains the CRM itself** — contacts, accounts, pipeline, relationship history — from meetings, email, and messaging, with no manual data entry; users keep "fingers lightly on the wheel" with override ability (https://www.bvp.com/atlas/lessons-from-day-ais-journey-to-becoming-the-waymo-of-crm, https://sequoiacap.com/podcast/training-data-christopher-odonnell/, https://www.day.ai/resources/building-the-ai-native-crm-at-day-ai). Founded by Christopher O'Donnell (ex-HubSpot CPO). For startups it replaces the CRM entirely; for scaling companies it sits alongside an existing one (https://www.contentgrip.com/day-ai-raises-20m-autonomous-crm/).

**Configuration:** Minimal-config by design (connect email/calendar/meetings; the system infers structure) — the opposite of Momentum's admin pipelines. Detailed public docs are thin; uncertainty flagged.

**Pricing:** Charges **per AI assistant**, recently shifted to a hybrid of seats + usage credits for heavy users (https://www.upstartsmedia.com/p/day-ai-sequoia-ai-crm; pricing page: https://day.ai/pricing). Exact figures not verified.

**Traction:** $20M Series A led by Sequoia (Pat Grady on board), announced Feb 2026, with Greenoaks, Conviction, Sound Ventures; ~**120 customers** after a year-plus of private testing — very early (https://www.upstartsmedia.com/p/day-ai-sequoia-ai-crm, https://pulse2.com/day-ai-20-million-series-a/).

---

## 7. Granola

**What it automates post-call:** Notes-first, automation-second. Notes/action items ready at meeting end; **"Recipes"** (launched late Sept 2025) are repeatable "/" prompts for post-call workflows like drafting follow-ups (https://www.granola.ai/, https://sacra.com/c/granola/). Native **CRM sync to HubSpot, Affinity, Attio** (notably *not* native Salesforce — Zapier only), pushing enhanced notes and action-item commitments into engagement records (https://www.granola.ai/blog/hubspot-meeting-notes-integration, https://www.coffee.ai/articles/integrate-granola-with-crm). No autonomous CRM field writes, no MEDDIC extraction, no bot in the call (audio captured device-side).

**Configuration:** Rep/individual-level (personal Recipes, personal templates); CRM integrations gated to Business/Enterprise plans — light admin surface (https://www.granola.ai/blog/granola-pricing-plans-features-roi).

**Pricing:** Free tier; Business ~$14/user/mo (CRM integrations, team folders); Enterprise $35+/user/mo (SSO) (https://www.granola.ai/blog/granola-pricing-plans-features-roi).

**Traction:** $43M Series B at $250M (May 2025, NFDG; https://techcrunch.com/2025/05/14/ai-note-taking-app-granola-raises-43m-at-250m-valuation-launches-collaborative-features/), then **$125M Series C at $1.5B valuation (March 25, 2026, Index Ventures + Kleiner Perkins)** — a 6x markup in ~10 months; positioning shift from notetaker to "enterprise company memory"; customers include Cursor (https://techcrunch.com/2026/03/25/granola-raises-125m-hits-1-5b-valuation-as-it-expands-from-meeting-notetaker-to-enterprise-ai-app/, https://sifted.eu/articles/ai-notetaking-startup-granola-hits-unicorn-status). Granola is loved by founders/PMs; it is *not* primarily a sales post-call automation tool.

---

## 8. Fireflies.ai

**What it automates post-call:** Transcription, summaries, action items; converts action items into **HubSpot tasks**; auto-pushes summaries/action items/deal data into **Salesforce and HubSpot** records; auto-posts recaps to Slack; 60+ native integrations (https://fireflies.ai/integrations/crm/hubspot, https://fireflies.ai/integrations). This is sync/logging automation, not judgment-based field updates (no MEDDIC-style structured extraction as a headline feature).

**Configuration:** Per-workspace admin settings for auto-join and integrations; CRM sync gated to Business plan.

**Pricing (public):** Free / Pro $10 / **Business $19 (CRM sync unlocks here)** / Enterprise $39 per user/mo annual (https://sonix.ai/resources/fireflies-ai-pricing/, https://www.cloudeagle.ai/blogs/blogs-fireflies-ai-pricing-guide).

**Traction:** Standout capital efficiency: ~$19M total raised, profitable since 2023, **$1B valuation via June 2025 tender offer** (not a primary round), self-reported 20M+ users across 500K+ orgs (https://fireflies.ai/blog/fireflies-1-billion-valuation/ — self-reported user figures). G2 4.8/5 (~735+ reviews); praise: transcription accuracy, integration depth; complaints: aggressive bot auto-join into private meetings, confusing free-tier credits, billing/cancellation friction on Trustpilot (https://www.g2.com/products/fireflies-ai/reviews, https://tldv.io/blog/fireflies-review/).

---

## 9. Fathom

**What it automates post-call:** Summaries, AI action items, **AI-drafted follow-up emails**, "Ask Fathom" chat; syncs notes/action items to Slack, Salesforce, HubSpot, Notion, Asana; Business tier adds **CRM field sync, deal views, coaching metrics, AI scorecards** (https://www.fathom.ai/, https://www.fathom.ai/overview, https://www.claap.io/blog/fathom-pricing). So: table-stakes automation plus light CRM-field automation at the top tier.

**Configuration:** Rep-level, free-tier-led (classic PLG); admin controls (retention, SSO, CRM field mapping) at Team/Business tiers.

**Pricing (public):** Generous free tier (premium AI features capped ~5 calls/mo); Premium $20/mo; Team $18/user/mo; Business $25/user/mo (CRM field sync, coaching) (https://www.meetjamie.ai/blog/fathom-ai-pricing, https://www.claap.io/blog/fathom-pricing).

**Traction:** $17M Series A Sep 2024 (Zoom among investors; ~$21.8M total — no Series B found as of this research: https://techcrunch.com/2024/09/19/ai-notetaker-fathom-raises-17m/, https://www.crunchbase.com/organization/fathom-video). Revenue $10M → $30M Aug 2024→Aug 2025 per CEO interview (https://getlatka.com/companies/fathom.ai — self-reported). HubSpot's **2025 Most Used App of the Year**, 20,000+ installs via HubSpot marketplace (https://ecosystem.hubspot.com/marketplace/listing/ai-notetaker-by-fathom). G2: top-rated; cons: free-tier caps, transcription drop-off in noisy/multilingual settings (https://www.g2.com/products/fathom-video/reviews).

---

# Synthesis: Table-stakes vs. Differentiators

## Table-stakes (2026) — nobody pays a premium for these anymore
- **Transcription, summaries, action-item extraction.** Explicitly called commoditized by multiple market participants: "transcription accuracy is a solved problem… summary quality is now table stakes" (https://wealthtechtoday.com/2025/04/29/best-ai-notetakers-for-financial-advisors-2025-a-strategic-buyers-guide/); Laxis's market report lists action items, CRM integration, and post-meeting workflow automation as baseline expectations sales platforms are "no longer viable" without (https://www.laxis.com/blog/state-of-meeting-note-taking-2026/).
- **Basic CRM logging** (attach notes/summary to the right contact/deal) — free-to-$25/user territory (Fathom, Fireflies pricing above). Fathom gives most of it away free; Fireflies gates it at $19.
- **Slack recap posting** and follow-up email *drafts* — every vendor in this list ships them, including HubSpot natively (Smart Deal Progression) and Gong (AI Composer, included free with licenses).
- **Enterprise hygiene**: SOC 2, no-training clauses, retention controls (Laxis report above).

The strongest structural evidence: **Gong bundles all 18 agents into existing licenses at no extra cost** (https://www.gong.io/press/gong-redefines-ai-agents-to-deliver-real-revenue-impact) and **HubSpot builds post-call CRM suggestions into the CRM itself** — when the two category gorillas price a capability at zero, it's table-stakes by definition.

## Differentiators — what still commands money
1. **Trusted autonomous CRM writes with policy controls.** Momentum's trigger + save-behavior model (confirm / write-if-empty / fully-automatic) into *any* Salesforce field/object is the clearest productization of "let the AI write to the CRM without wrecking it" (https://docs.momentum.io/autopilot). HubSpot's version stops at "suggested" updates — the autonomy gap is the differentiator.
2. **Methodology-specific extraction** (MEDDIC/MEDDPICC/BANT into real CRM fields) — Momentum markets a dedicated product for it (https://www.momentum.io/meddic-autopilot); Gong's AI Deal Reviewer scores against methodologies but doesn't primarily write fields. This is a RevOps-buyer feature, sold top-down.
3. **Multi-step, cross-system chains** (call → fields + case + Snowflake + Slack + email) rather than single actions — Momentum, Attention; Gong is heading there with trigger-based auto-briefs (June 2026 release notes).
4. **Institutional memory / cross-call intelligence** — Gong Ask Anything/Deep Researcher, Granola's "company memory" pivot; described as what moves tools "from 'write less' to 'the company's living memory'" (https://www.assemblyai.com/blog/ai-notetakers-beyond-transcription-how-leading-companies-turn-meetings-into-measurable-business-value).
5. **CRM replacement itself** (Day.ai's bet): if conversations auto-generate the system of record, post-call automation ceases to be a feature. Earliest-stage, ~120 customers — unproven but the most heavily backed thesis per dollar (Sequoia).

## What buyers actually pay for / what churns — evidence
- **Buyers resist per-seat and per-conversation AI pricing; vendors are converging on pay-per-outcome.** Salesforce was forced off $2/conversation to $0.10/action Flex Credits after "confusion and backlash" (https://www.getmonetizely.com/blogs/the-doomed-evolution-of-salesforces-agentforce-pricing, https://www.salesforce.com/news/press-releases/2025/05/15/agentforce-flexible-pricing-news/); HubSpot moved to $0.50 per *resolved* conversation / $1 per qualified lead (https://www.hubspot.com/company-news/hubspots-customer-agent-and-prospecting-agent-now-you-pay-when-the-task-is-complete). Two independent repricings in 12 months is the strongest market signal in this research.
- **Agentforce is the documented under-performer:** only ~6% of Salesforce customers on *paid* Agentforce, and slower adoption cited in below-consensus FY26 guidance (https://www.salesforceben.com/where-are-we-really-at-with-agentforce-adoption/) — though 60% of recent bookings being expansions suggests survivors are getting value (https://www.salesforceben.com/agentforce-customers-are-doubling-down-60-of-q4-bookings-came-from-expansions/).
- **Price-anchored churn pressure on Gong:** consistent G2/analyst complaints about $5K–$50K platform fees, forced bundles, 5–15% auto-renewal escalators; cheap notetakers (Fathom/Fireflies at $0–25) are explicitly marketed as Gong-displacement, and ~40% of Gong customers still buy Clari on top (https://www.sybill.ai/blogs/gong-pricing, https://www.oliv.ai/blog/gong-io-pricing — note: mostly competitor-authored sources, but the pattern is consistent across several).
- **What retains: workflow embedding, not model quality.** SaaStr's analysis of coming AI-agent churn: "prompts are portable… deep workflow embedding creates real friction, not because the AI is better, but because the plumbing is harder to replicate" (https://www.saastr.com/the-wave-of-ai-agent-churn-to-come-prompts-are-portable/). Consistent with who's winning: Fireflies (profitable, $1B, integration-depth moat), Fathom (distribution moat via HubSpot marketplace), Momentum (RevOps plumbing into Salesforce), vs. thin "AI layer" tools.
- **Two viable commercial poles, hollow middle:** bottom-up cheap/freemium notetakers with CRM sync (Fathom $30M rev on ~$22M raised; Fireflies profitable since 2023) and top-down RevOps automation platforms (Momentum, Attention, Gong) sold on pipeline-hygiene ROI. Mid-priced standalone "AI sales assistant" seats without either distribution or deep CRM plumbing show the weakest evidence of durable traction.

**Key uncertainties:** Gong's $500M ARR / 55% growth is self-reported and unusually high — unverified. Attention and Momentum pricing figures are third-party estimates. Day.ai capability detail is largely from founder interviews/press, not documentation. Smart Deal Progression (HubSpot) is still public beta with unpublished pricing.

# Solela: Product Overview

**What it is:**
Solela is a personal AI assistant designed across multiple interfaces—web, WhatsApp, and Skills—that maintains unified memory across all platforms. It handles tasks across four life domains: personal assistance, shopping, travel, and work.

**Positioning:**
The product emphasizes accessibility and privacy. The tagline captures its core promise: "One AI. Four lives. The same memory — anywhere you write." It positions itself as built for people who already write frequently, distinguishing itself through integrated memory rather than disconnected tools.

**Privacy by Architecture:**
Rather than bolting on security measures, Solela embeds privacy into its design. Key architectural claims include:

- "Isolated containers, logged actions, nothing sent without your tap"
- "OS-level isolation per agent. No noisy neighbours"
- "Credentials never leak" (Keys reside in a gateway, not with the agent)
- "Your assistant lives in its own container. Nobody else, ever"
- "Full audit trail" of all prompts and changes
- "Cross-workspace reads are architecturally impossible"

**Onboarding Flow:**
Three simple steps: "Sign in" via Google, "Name it" to create a private container, then "Start writing" on the web or WhatsApp. The company targets "Sixty seconds, start to finish" with no payment required upfront.

# Adjacent-Space Research Report: "One Agent Per Employee" Landscape (2025–2026)

Compiled July 2026 from five parallel research streams, ~130 web sources. Every claim carries a source URL; vendor-reported numbers are labeled; uncertainty flagged inline. Solela.ai was independently re-verified by direct fetch before finalizing.

---

## 1. "Digital employee / AI coworker" products — does the category work?

### Per-product summary

**11x.ai (Alice, AI SDR)** — Outbound SDR "digital worker." Sales-led onboarding (2–4 weeks ICP/email-infra setup); pricing from ~$36K/yr per its own page (https://www.11x.ai/products/alice/pricing). **The category's cautionary tale**: TechCrunch's March 2025 investigation (https://techcrunch.com/2025/03/24/a16z-and-benchmark-backed-11x-has-been-claiming-customers-it-doesnt-have/) found inflated ARR (contracts with 3-month break clauses counted as full ARR; one employee estimated only ~$3M of $14M reported ARR survived trials), logo misuse (ZoomInfo threatened legal action, said the product "performed significantly worse than our SDR employees"; Airtable never went past a short trial), and employee-reported **70–80% customer churn**. Founder Hasan Sukkar stepped down as CEO in May 2025; still operating under CTO-turned-CEO Prabhav Jain (https://toarn.com/insights/11x-ai — single secondary source for details; CEO change widely reported).

**Artisan (Ava, AI BDR)** — Outbound BDR with standard white-glove onboarding (dedicated AM, 2–4 weeks) (https://www.artisan.co/pricing). Quote-based pricing; third parties report ~$1.5K–$5K+/mo for real BDR replacement (unverified). $25M Series A April 2025 (https://techcrunch.com/2025/04/09/artisan-the-stop-hiring-humans-ai-agent-startup-raises-25m-and-is-still-hiring-humans/); self-reported ~$5–6M ARR — modest revenue relative to the enormous noise of the "Stop Hiring Humans" rage-bait campaign (which generated ~$2M ARR and death threats: https://sfstandard.com/2025/04/07/the-real-person-behind-san-franciscos-hated-anti-human-ad-campaign/). Reported LinkedIn account restrictions for automation/spam are a structural product risk (single-source, unverified: https://completeaitraining.com/news/from-stop-hiring-humans-to-linkedin-bans-artisan-ais-viral/). Reviewer consensus: an email-volume machine; personalization is template-grade.

**Maisa AI** — Not an SDR: auditable "digital workers" for compliance-sensitive back-office processes, explicitly counter-positioned against the "95% of AI pilots fail" narrative. Self-serve "Maisa Studio" where citizen developers train workers in natural language. $25M seed Aug 2025 (https://techcrunch.com/2025/08/27/maisa-ai-gets-25m-to-fix-enterprise-ais-95-failure-rate/); Tracxn lists a May 2026 Series A (amount unconfirmed). No public pricing, no independent efficacy evidence yet.

**Piper (Qualified)** — Inbound AI SDR (website visitors → qualified meetings); requires Salesforce; ~$40–68K/yr per third parties (https://www.knock-ai.com/blog/qualified-pricing). 500+ customers incl. Box, Brex, Asana (vendor-reported). **The category's cleanest success: Salesforce agreed to acquire Qualified in Dec 2025** (https://www.saastr.com/why-salesforce-acquiring-qualified-is-maybe-the-smartest-ai-gtm-deal-of-2025/). Key lesson: it succeeded on a *bounded* task (qualifying warm inbound), not open-ended judgment.

**Beam.ai** — Back-office agentic process automation; template-led onboarding; ~$299 entry (single source, unverified). Low public signal either way — no controversy, no independent evidence of scale (https://beam.ai/, https://www.selecthub.com/p/ai-agent-builder-software/beam-ai/).

**Ema (ema.co)** — "Universal AI Employee" via pre-built Personas (support, HR, sales, legal); no-code builder, enterprise motion, on-prem options. $61M+ raised (Accel/Section 32: https://venturebeat.com/ai/ema-raises-36m-to-build-universal-ai-employees-for-enterprises); GetLatka estimates ~$15M 2025 revenue (unverified). Mid-pack; efficacy claims entirely vendor-sourced.

**Lyzr** — Really an agent-infrastructure platform ("Agentic OS") with "AI employees" marketing; IT/developer-led onboarding. $14.5M Series A+ led by Accenture at $250M valuation, reported >300% QoQ revenue growth from a small base (https://finovate.com/agentic-ai-infrastructure-firm-lyzr-ai-raises-14-5-million-at-250-million-valuation/).

**Cykel AI (Lucy/Eve/Samson)** — LSE-listed named digital workers. The audited numbers are damning: **£4,107 revenue in the half-year to July 2025** (not a typo), £1.2M pretax loss, shares down 29% on results (https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/cykel-ai-narrows-interim-loss-slashes-administrative-expenses). The starkest narrative-vs-reality gap in the category.

**MultiOn → Please** — The autonomous web-agent pioneer split and pivoted hard: founder Div Garg left Dec 2024 to found AGI Inc.; the company rebranded to Please Platforms and is now, verified directly, a consumer **"thinking reminders app"** in research preview (https://please.ai). A quiet negative data point for general-purpose autonomous agents.

**Devin (Cognition)** — The paradox. Independently measured early performance was poor: Answer.AI's month-long review scored **3 successes / 14 failures / 3 inconclusive** on 20 real tasks ("tasks it can do are so small and well-defined that I may as well do them myself": https://www.answer.ai/posts/2025-01-08-devin.html), and the launch Upwork demo was debunked (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=40008109). Yet commercially: ARR $1M → $73M (Sep 2024→Jun 2025, Sacra), Windsurf acquisition, $10.2B valuation Sep 2025 (https://www.cnbc.com/2025/09/08/cognition-valued-at-10point2-billion-two-months-after-windsurf-.html), then **$1B+ raise at ~$25B pre-money May 2026** (https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/27/ai-coding-startup-cognition-raises-1b-at-25b-pre-money-valuation/). Pricing dropped from $500/mo to a $20/mo usage-based entry tier.

### Category verdict

- **The fully-autonomous AI SDR wave of 2024–25 broadly failed**: analyst posts report 50–70% annual churn for AI SDR tools and reply-rate decay as buyers pattern-match AI templates (https://www.digitalapplied.com/blog/case-against-ai-sdrs-contrarian-analysis-2026 — directionally consistent across sources, individually unaudited). AI-app retention is structurally worse than SaaS (~21% vs ~31% annual: https://www.technewsworld.com/story/ai-apps-generate-revenue-but-struggle-with-retention-180236.html).
- **Winners are bounded-task, verifiable-output products** (Devin: code compiles or doesn't; Piper: warm inbound qualification). **Losers sold headcount replacement on open-ended judgment** (11x, Cykel, MultiOn).
- The "digital employee" *metaphor* looks like a 2024 marketing artifact; surviving products are sold as tools with narrow measurable outcomes, humans in the loop, and the capability is being absorbed into existing sales stacks as a feature layer.

**Implication for NanoCo**: the vision — agent as *amplifier of an employee* rather than *replacement of an employee* — sits on the correct side of the documented failure line. The failures were all "fire the human"; nobody on this list productizes "one agent per employee that makes the employee better."

### Table-stakes vs differentiating (the market's answer)

**Table-stakes (free-to-$25/user, nobody pays a premium):** transcription, summaries, action items, follow-up email *drafts*, Slack recaps, basic CRM note logging. Structural proof: Gong bundles all 18 agents at no extra cost and HubSpot builds suggested post-call CRM updates into the CRM natively — when both gorillas price it at zero, it's table-stakes (https://www.laxis.com/blog/state-of-meeting-note-taking-2026/ corroborates).

**Differentiating (what still commands money):**
1. **Trusted autonomous CRM writes with policy controls** — Momentum's confirm/write-if-empty/full-auto save policies; HubSpot stops at "suggested," and that autonomy gap is the value line.
2. **Methodology-specific extraction** (MEDDIC/BANT into real fields) — a RevOps, top-down sale.
3. **Multi-step cross-system chains** (call → fields + case + Slack + email + warehouse).
4. **Institutional memory across calls** (Gong Ask Anything, Granola's pivot).

**Buyer-behavior signals:** two forced repricings in 12 months (Salesforce off per-conversation, HubSpot to pay-per-result) show buyers resist paying for AI *activity* and will pay for *outcomes*. Retention correlates with workflow embedding, not model quality — "prompts are portable… the plumbing is harder to replicate" (https://www.saastr.com/the-wave-of-ai-agent-churn-to-come-prompts-are-portable/).

**Implication for NanoCo**: the post-sales-call *chain* itself (summary → follow-up → CRM) is commoditized. What's not commoditized: methodology-aware extraction personally calibrated to the rep, and graduated write-autonomy — which is exactly the Momentum policy model generalized. Note Momentum's shipped confirm/write-if-empty/auto controls as prior art.

## 3. Onboarding-by-interview / calibration patterns + solela.ai

### solela.ai — VERIFIED, exists and is live
Independently confirmed by direct fetch of https://www.solela.ai/ (plus https://elion.solela.ai/). A personal AI assistant across web/WhatsApp/Skills with unified memory ("One AI. Four lives. The same memory — anywhere you write"). Positioning is explicitly **"Privacy by architecture"**, verbatim claims: "OS-level isolation per agent. No noisy neighbours," "Keys live in a gateway. The agent never sees them," "Approval before action," "Full audit trail," "Cross-workspace reads are architecturally impossible." Onboarding is ~60 seconds, three steps (Google sign-in → "Name it" → start writing on web/WhatsApp) — **notably no interview/calibration step is advertised**. No independent press, funding, or reviews found; company scale unverified. Do not conflate with a16z-backed Sola (sola.ai).

### The three calibration patterns in the market
1. **Interview-first** (rare): **Dot (New Computer)** was the purest consumer example — onboarding asked getting-to-know-you questions and probed deeper to build a psychological profile (https://techcrunch.com/2024/06/21/dots-ai-really-really-wants-to-get-to-know-you/) — **and it shut down Oct 2025** (https://techcrunch.com/2025/09/05/personalized-ai-companion-app-dot-is-shutting-down/). **OpenAI GPT Builder** is the canonical "agent interviews you, then writes its own config" mechanism (https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8770868-gpt-builder). Coaching products do it well: **BetterUp** (2–3 min intake survey + Whole Person Assessment), **Rocky.ai** (goal/obstacle intake), **Valence Nadia** (calibration *through* conversation; generates a user-controlled "collaboration profile" other Nadias can read — https://www.bvp.com/news/meet-nadia-valences-ai-coach-for-leadership-development-and-workplace-collaboration).
2. **Template/segmentation-first** (dominant): **Lindy** asks role/industry, then lands you on role-matched templates with a working example (https://obviostudio.substack.com/p/ai-integration-lindy-from-onboarding); **Zapier Agents** builds config from a natural-language description via a prompt assistant.
3. **Ingestion/ambient-first**: **Martin** (connect email/calendar, memory built through use), **ohai.ai** (forms + forward-your-emails), **Yohana** (human-guide intake — the concierge analog; medium confidence, pages partially unreachable), **Solela** (name it and go).

### What retains non-technical users (UX research)
- Analysis of 150+ AI onboarding flows: nearly all successful products converged on **template activation loops**; blank canvas kills conversion; **generated editable drafts beat static templates** (https://www.fishmanafnewsletter.com/p/how-ai-products-drive-adoption-in-onboarding-through-template-activation-loop).
- Wow moment within ~3 minutes; light role/goal questions make users feel it's "built for someone like you," but long interviews are absent from winners (https://www.growthmates.news/p/what-ai-products-get-right-and-wrong). Sub-60-second activation is the emerging bar (https://productled.com/blog/ai-onboarding).
- The Valence/Gilead deployment finding: getting users into a live session within 10 minutes — where participants "felt Nadia was getting to know them" — produced the aha (https://www.valence.co/ai-and-the-workforce/how-gilead-sciences-is-scaling-ai-coaching-to-all-employees-kerry-okeeffe-gilead-valence).

**Implication for NanoCo**: a long upfront self-profiling interview is empirically risky (Dot died; winners activate in minutes). The evidence-backed hybrid: 1–3 light calibration questions + a role template that produces a *working draft workflow immediately*, with the deep profiling interview woven into the first real work sessions (Nadia model) rather than gating them.

## 4. Graduated trust / expanding autonomy

**Bottom line: graduated trust exists as vocabulary and process everywhere, as an automated product mechanism almost nowhere.**

- **What's shipped is static:** per-step approval toggles (Lindy HITL confirmations — https://docs.lindy.ai/testing/human-in-the-loop; Relay.app's approval/data-input/AI-output-review steps — https://docs.relay.app/human-in-the-loop/human-in-the-loop-steps; Zapier pause-for-review; LangGraph `interrupt` per-tool approve/edit/reject) and discrete global modes (Claude Code's default/plan/acceptEdits/bypass; Devin CLI modes; OpenAI Operator's fixed auto/watch/human-only tiers keyed to site sensitivity — https://openai.com/index/introducing-operator/). Microsoft's Agent 365 / Copilot Studio governance is org-level control of which agents exist, not per-agent graduation (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot/blog/copilot-studio/new-and-improved-agent-governance-intelligent-workflows-and-connected-app-experiences/).
- **Closest shipped approximations:** (1) **Cursor Auto-review** (June 2026) — a classifier in the execution path modulates freedom per action, marketed as "autonomy is a dial, not a switch"; blocks ~4% of actions, cut user interruptions from ~40% to ~7% (https://cursor.com/blog/agent-autonomy-auto-review) — but it's *contextual*, not *earned over time*. (2) Claude Code's persistent allowlists — the envelope widens with tenure, but by manual grants. (3) Decagon's percentage-of-traffic ramps + shadow mode in support AI (https://decagon.ai/blog/ai-customer-support-setup) — real graduation, human-decided. (4) Momentum's confirm/write-if-empty/auto save policies (section 2).
- **Frameworks exist and are current:** Feng/McDonald/Zhang, "Levels of Autonomy for AI Agents" (arXiv June 2025) — five SAE-style levels defined by user role (Operator→Observer), plus a proposed "autonomy certificates" governance mechanism (https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12469). Enterprise playbooks converge on "autonomy must be earned": Microsoft SOC crawl-walk-run guide; ManageEngine ("expand execution privileges only after reversal rates decline").
- **The key empirical datum:** Anthropic's "Measuring AI agent autonomy in practice" (Feb 2026) — full auto-approve appears in ~20% of new users' sessions vs >40% at 750+ sessions, with oversight shifting from approval to monitoring (https://www.anthropic.com/research/measuring-agent-autonomy). **Earned trust demonstrably happens — in the user, not in the product.**
- **No verified shipped product implements automatic earned autonomy** (permission scope widening automatically as track record improves — e.g., auto-promotion after N clean approvals). This is an absence-of-evidence finding after targeted search, not proof of nonexistence.

**Implication for NanoCo**: "guardrails that expand as trust grows" — if made *mechanical* (track-record-gated promotion from suggest → auto-with-review → auto, per action type, visible to both employee and org) — is genuine whitespace with academic legitimation (autonomy-certificates paper) and behavioral validation (Anthropic data). It is a real differentiator; per-step approval toggles alone are not.

## Answers to the four key questions

**(a) What onboarding UX retains non-technical users?** Not a long interview. The converged winning pattern: role-based template + generated editable draft + wow-moment inside ~3 minutes; deep calibration deferred into the first real work sessions where the user *feels* the agent getting to know them (Valence/Gilead). Dot — the purest interview-first product — is dead. NanoCo's self-profiling interview should produce a visibly working workflow fast, then keep interviewing incrementally.

**(b) What does the sales market treat as proven value?** Table-stakes: transcription/summary/action-items/follow-up drafts/Slack recaps (priced at ~zero by Gong and HubSpot). Proven paid value: trusted autonomous CRM writes with policy controls, methodology-specific field extraction (MEDDIC etc.), and multi-step cross-system chains — sold to RevOps on pipeline-hygiene ROI. Buyers are forcing outcome-based pricing (two major repricings in 12 months). Retention comes from workflow embedding, not model quality.

**(c) Is "role methodology packs, personally calibrated" occupied?** Substantially whitespace as a combination. Pieces exist: Gong's AI Deal Reviewer scores against methodologies; Momentum extracts MEDDIC to fields; Ema sells role Personas; coaching products calibrate to the person. Nobody found combines *role methodology encoded as multi-step workflows at core moments* + *personal calibration via interview* + *one persistent agent per employee*. Closest structural analogs are admin-configured RevOps tools (team-level, not person-level) — the person-level calibration is the open slot. Caveat: the "digital employee" graveyard (section 1) shows the framing must stay "amplifier," not "replacement."

**(d) Is graduated-trust guardrails a real differentiator?** Yes — with precision. Per-step approvals and mode toggles are commodity. What no verified product ships is *automatic earned autonomy*: permission scope that widens mechanically with a clean track record. The demand is documented (enterprise playbooks all preach it), the behavior is measured (Anthropic: auto-approve doubles with user tenure), the framework is published (arXiv 2506.12469 "autonomy certificates") — and the mechanism is unbuilt. That, plus the fact that it doubles as the employee-development mechanic (earning your agent more autonomy *is* the skill ladder — question 5's whitespace), makes it arguably NanoCo's most defensible differentiator, since it uniquely fuses two gaps no one else connects.

**Biggest overall caveat:** many category-level statistics (AI SDR churn rates, several ARR figures) come from vendor-adjacent content marketing — directionally corroborated across independent sources but individually unaudited; all such figures are flagged inline above.
